WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"At that time Berodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present unto Hezekiah: for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick." 2 Kings 20:12
Isaiah's account: "he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered". Isaiah 39:1
Chronicles speaks of "the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sent unto him to enquire of the wonder that was done in the land". 2 Chronicles 32:31
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Chronicles: in the business of the ambassadors "God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart". 2 Chronicles 32:31
Letters and a present for Hezekiah; Hezekiah "hearkened unto them" (Kings) or "was glad of them" (Isaiah). 2 Kings 20:12–13 Isaiah 39:2
Isaiah foretold that some of Hezekiah's own sons would serve as eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace. 2 Kings 20:18

Wars, works and turning points

The prophets who spoke about him
Is Isaiah son of Amoz “all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store unto this day, shall be carried into Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the LORD.”

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
ROGERS (1912)
Proclaimed king at the New Year of 721 BC; twelve years, until Sargon drove him out. A second reign of nine months by the Babylonian king list, which Rogers places in 702 BC.
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Scripture gives no years for him (2 Kgs 20:12; Isa 39:1).
PTOLEMY'S CANON
Twelve years from 721 BC (Rogers's table).
LUMBY (1887)
No years given[52]
Driven out in 709 BC; back on the throne in 702 BC for a brief time.
After the illness
2 Kings 20:12; Isaiah 39:1
"At that time", when he heard Hezekiah had been sick and had recovered. 2 Kings 20:12 Isaiah 39:1
In his first reign, before Sargon drove him out
the Pulpit Commentary (1880–97)
Merodach-baladan held Babylon against Sargon from 722 BC and sent the embassy probably hoping for an alliance with Hezekiah, also an enemy of Sargon. 2 Kings 20:12 [46]
In his short second reign
R. W. Rogers (1912); Ellicott's commentary, following Schrader
Rogers: when he retook Babylon, "His first move was to send an embassy to Hezekiah"; Ellicott's commentary says "perhaps" it was then, during a brief reign of six months. 2 Kings 20:12 [82][8]
It depends on the date of the illness
J. R. Lumby (1887)
If Hezekiah's illness came before Sennacherib's invasion, the embassy belongs to the long first reign; if after, to the brief second one. 2 Kings 20:1 2 Kings 20:12 [52]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture says nothing of Merodach-baladan's wars with Assyria or of how long he reigned.
Scripture does not say what answer the envoys took back to Babylon.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textKings spells his name Berodach-baladan and Isaiah Merodach-baladan; both call him "the son of Baladan, king of Babylon". 2 Kings 20:12 Isaiah 39:1
Scholars' viewHe is the Marduk-apal-iddina (Merodach-baladan) of the Assyrian and Babylonian records, as Luckenbill's and Rogers's translations render the name.[30][72]

links.text: Gedaliah, Governor of Judah under Babylon
Belshazzar, King of Babylon, as Daniel calls him
Tirhakah, King of Ethiopia (Cush), Scripture gives no years. It names him twice, in one report, as "king of Ethiopia" (2 Kgs 19:9; Isa 37:9)., c. 690–664 BC, no
Shalmaneser, King of Assyria, Scripture gives no length for his reign. It places him in the reigns of Hoshea of Israel and Hezekiah of Judah., c. 727–722 BC, no
Menahem, King of Israel, Ten years in Samaria (2 Kings 15:17), c. 752–742 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
Pekahiah, King of Israel, Two years (2 Kings 15:23), c. 742–740 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
